title: Keep contact available during an outage
problem: When the public settings requests fail, the contact page loses the email address and phone number.
impact: A visitor cannot reach Giulia at the moment they decide to enquire.
change: Keep verified contact details in the local site profile. Show them immediately, independently of galleries and settings requests.
benefit: An enquiry route remains available during a service interruption.
dependency: Owner confirms the fallback contact details.
proof: Phase 1 controlled network failure; this is not a claim of current downtime.

title: Make room for the first action on mobile
problem: The privacy panel occupies about 464 px of an 844 px screen and covers the session action.
impact: The visitor meets a large decision panel before understanding the offer.
change: Use a short, in-flow privacy strip with equally visible choices and a separate explanation. Keep the hero action above it.
benefit: The offer, session action and privacy choices can all be seen together.
dependency: Retain the existing consent rules and preference storage.

title: Replace the portfolio dead end with real work
problem: The first navigation destination opens an empty portfolio.
impact: People looking for evidence of the photographic style find no work to assess.
change: Curate an approved selection. The mockup demonstrates a layout with existing public session images; it does not invent client galleries.
benefit: Visitors can assess the visual style before contacting Giulia.
dependency: Owner approves the selection, publication rights and collection links.
proof: Reclassified from P0 to P1: this is a serious dead end, but contact is still reachable.

title: Give the family offer its own clear shape
problem: The family session has no duration or price; its inclusions also list couple and maternity sessions sold separately.
impact: Visitors cannot tell which offer fits their needs or compare it fairly.
change: Make the family benefit and next step concise. Keep the price absent until the owner supplies it; confirm the boundaries of the offer.
benefit: A clearer enquiry without fabricated prices or promises.
dependency: Owner supplies scope, duration and pricing.

title: Replace the unnamed service area
problem: The contact page refers to 50 km around “this region” without naming the region.
impact: Visitors cannot confidently judge whether their location is covered.
change: Invite visitors to include their city. Publish a specific coverage statement only after confirmation; use Rive-Sud travel wording only where it already appears in an offer.
benefit: Fewer assumptions about travel and location.
dependency: Owner confirms the service area and travel terms.

title: Let visitors compare birthday packages first
problem: A long introduction precedes the three packages and the contact action.
impact: Mobile visitors must read or scroll extensively to find the practical information.
change: Lead with a short summary, existing prices and durations. Show three scannable packages, then the detailed story and terms.
benefit: The cost, fit and next step are easier to compare.
dependency: Preserve the published tariff content and confirm tax wording.

title: Bring the email into the first screen
problem: A large heading and introduction push the email action near the bottom of the initial phone screen.
impact: The route to an enquiry takes unnecessary searching and scrolling.
change: Put email and phone directly under a short heading. Carry the chosen session into the email subject.
benefit: A shorter, clearer route from interest to conversation.
dependency: Use the verified email and phone already on the public site.

title: Name the sessions in the home selector
problem: The five dots are accessible controls, but their visible appearance does not explain what comes next.
impact: Visitors may miss relevant sessions or think the site has only one offer.
change: Add a compact named session selector and a visible position indicator. Keep the approved immersive format.
benefit: Visitors can deliberately choose an offer.
dependency: Use the existing enabled and show-on-home settings; do not enable /services automatically.

title: Give white hero text a reliable backdrop
problem: White text crosses bright parts of the photograph; legibility changes with the crop.
impact: The title and supporting copy can be difficult to read.
change: Place text in a calm area with a consistent dark scrim; verify every slide and crop, including focus states.
benefit: More dependable readability while keeping photography dominant.
dependency: Check contrast against the actual image pixels at each breakpoint.
proof: A visual risk observed in the capture, not a completed WCAG conformance test.

title: Carry the brand rhythm into interior pages
problem: Heavy interior headings and some generic interface treatments feel disconnected from the restrained photographic home.
change: Use the existing Playfair face for expressive headings, a clear sans for reading, consistent spacing and a warm visible focus outline.
benefit: A more coherent and readable brand experience.
dependency: Extend shared semantic tokens and typed components during implementation.

title: Retire the preparation notice when ready
problem: A permanent preparation notice consumes scarce mobile space and makes the experience feel unfinished.
change: Remove it only after contact resilience, approved imagery and offer content are ready. Mockups show this ready state.
benefit: More room for the offer and a clearer sense of readiness.
dependency: A01, A03 and A04 readiness checks.

title: Promise a conversation, not instant booking
problem: A booking-style label leads to Contact, without an immediate reservation flow.
impact: The action sets an expectation the next page does not fulfill.
change: Use “Parlons de votre séance” and keep the genuine biography. Show the simple existing enquiry process nearby.
benefit: People understand what will happen next.
dependency: Keep FR and EN labels aligned; no booking integration is needed.

title: Polish the English offer labels
problem: The English catalogue includes “Portraits Photography” and inconsistent currency formatting.
impact: Small wording inconsistencies weaken the otherwise personal presentation.
change: Use “Portrait photography” and consistent CAD formatting. Review both languages together.
dependency: Use shared FR and EN resources.
proof: Catalogue finding. The French capture locates the component; switch the mockup to EN to inspect the proposed wording.

title: Decide what the About portrait communicates
problem: The current image has empty alternative text.
impact: If the portrait conveys useful identity information, a screen-reader visitor misses it.
change: Use a short factual description if it is informative; keep empty text if it is intentionally decorative. The mockup treats it as a portrait of Giulia.
benefit: Equivalent context without redundant image descriptions.
dependency: Confirm image purpose; empty alt alone is not evidence of a failure.

title: Measure the enquiry path after launch
problem: The audit found page views, but no verified session-to-enquiry measurement.
impact: It is difficult to tell whether the new hierarchy helps visitors.
change: After implementation, measure session opens and contact clicks only with consent. Test labels before trying experiments.
benefit: A way to evaluate the design; no conversion uplift is claimed.
dependency: Ship A02, A07 and A08 first; preserve consent and gallery exclusions.
proof: Instrumentation proposal, not a visible UI defect. The marker locates the action to measure.

title: Keep the action reachable on short screens
problem: At 320 × 568, the long introduction initially puts the action below the visible hero area.
impact: A small-screen visitor must discover an inner scroll before continuing.
change: Shorten the opening copy, reduce oversized spacing and keep the action in the first viewport after the privacy choice.
benefit: An obvious next step on compact phones.
dependency: Check short and landscape viewports as well as 390 px width.
proof: The current action is reachable by scrolling or focus; it is not completely inaccessible.

title: Align the shared-link image with the opening
problem: The configured social image differs from the first home session photograph.
impact: A shared link may set a different visual expectation.
change: Review both crops and use an approved image that represents the intended opening. The prototype demonstrates the family photograph.
benefit: A more consistent first impression across entry points.
dependency: Owner selects the sharing image and approves its crop.
proof: Consistency check, not a broken link or a fabricated social-network screenshot.
